text: Demoralization syndrome, characterized by distress and subjective incompetence, is prevalent among cancer survivors and particularly salient among breast cancer survivors (BCS). Collective trauma may exacerbate existential vulnerability and heighten demoralization syndrome. However, no study has compared demoralization syndrome among BCS and non-BCS women exposed to the same war-related context, nor examined age as a moderator of this relationship. Therefore, this study aimed to: (a) compare levels and clinically significant prevalence of demoralization syndrome between BCS and non-BCS women exposed to the October 7 war; (b) examine the association between war exposure and demoralization syndrome in both groups; and (c) test whether this association was moderated by breast cancer survivorship status and age.
source_label: Demoralization syndrome among women exposed to war: comparing breast cancer survivors and those with no breast cancer history
